question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{21{x}^{2}y}{2}, & \,-1<x\le 0,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expression of the conditional probability density function ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ for $-1<x\le 0,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 1.$
question.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the marginal density function for $X,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}\frac{21{x}^{2}y}{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{21{x}^{2}}{2}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}y\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{21{x}^{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{{y}^{2}}{2}\,{|}_{{x}^{2}}^{1} \\  & =\frac{21{x}^{2}}{4}\cdot (1-{x}^{4}) \\  & =\frac{21{x}^{2}(1-{x}^{4})}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the following:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{21{x}^{2}(1-{x}^{4})}{4}, & \,-1<x\le 0 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)},
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal density function for $X.$

Now, for $-1<x\le 0,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 1,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{21{x}^{2}y}{2})}{(\frac{21{x}^{2}(1-{x}^{4})}{4})} \\  & =\frac{2y}{1-{x}^{4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2y}{1-{x}^{4}}, & \,-1<x\le 0,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
